title: Portugal Digital Nomad Visa 2026: Singapore Guide
metaDescription: Portugal digital nomad visa D8 2026 for Singapore applicants: €3,680 monthly income, 3-month average, documents, AIMA permit and tax notes explained.
headline: Portugal Digital Nomad Visa 2026: Singapore Guide

sections.title: What is the Portugal digital nomad visa?
sections.content:
Portugal's digital nomad visa, commonly called the D8, is a residence visa for non-EU remote employees, freelancers and business owners whose employers or clients are all outside Portugal. It is not for local Portuguese employment, and it is different from the D7 passive-income visa for pensions, rent and investment income.

The route starts with a four-month residence visa obtained at a Portuguese consulate or visa centre abroad, followed by conversion to a residence permit with AIMA after arrival. The residence permit is granted for two years and can then be renewed for three years at a time.

sections.title: Income requirement for 2026
sections.content:
For 2026, a single applicant must show average remote-work income of at least €3,680 per month over the last three months, which is four times Portugal's national minimum wage of €920. Consulates look at the three-month average, so steady income helps more than one unusually large month.

Family thresholds rise with household size: add about €460 per month for a spouse or partner and about €276 per month for each dependent child. Most consulates also expect savings of roughly €11,040, or twelve times the minimum wage, as a matter of practice, even though that figure is not the legal income test itself.

sections.title: Documents and application steps
sections.content:
Typical documents include a valid passport, proof of remote employment or freelance contracts, three months of income evidence, proof of accommodation in Portugal, travel insurance with at least €30,000 of coverage, and a recent criminal record certificate. Some consulates ask for a Portuguese tax number and a local bank account, so check the exact checklist for your consulate.

Apply at the consulate or VFS centre covering your legal residence, attend an appointment, and expect a decision in about 60 days in many cases. After arrival, book an AIMA appointment promptly to convert the visa into a residence permit, and keep copies of every document submitted.

sections.title: Tax, stay and long-term options
sections.content:
Living in Portugal on a D8 does not remove tax duties in your home country: United States citizens, for example, still file an annual return and report worldwide income. In Portugal, remote workers should take local tax advice early, because residence, social security and double-tax rules depend on personal circumstances.

After five years of legal residence, many holders can consider permanent residence, while citizenship timelines depend on the nationality law in force at the time. Rules changed in 2026, with a longer ten-year path reported for most non-EU nationals, so confirm the current law before planning around citizenship.

faqs.q: How much do you need to earn for Portugal's digital nomad visa in 2026?
faqs.a: In 2026 you need average remote-work income of at least €3,680 per month over the last three months, which is four times Portugal's minimum wage of €920. Add about €460 per month for a spouse or partner and about €276 per month for each child, and expect many consulates to also look for roughly €11,040 in savings.

faqs.q: Can you work for a Portuguese company on the D8 visa?
faqs.a: No, the D8 is for remote work for employers or clients outside Portugal, so local Portuguese employment does not qualify. If your income comes from pensions, rent or investments rather than remote work, the D7 passive-income visa is usually the better match, with a much lower income threshold.

faqs.q: How long is the Portugal digital nomad residence permit?
faqs.a: The consular residence visa lasts four months and allows two entries, and after arrival AIMA converts it into a residence permit valid for two years. That permit can then be renewed for three years at a time, provided you still meet the income, accommodation and insurance requirements.

faqs.q: Where do you apply for the Portugal D8 visa?
faqs.a: You apply at the Portuguese consulate, embassy or VFS Global office covering your legal residence, not from inside Portugal in most cases. Bring the full checklist for that consulate, because requirements for tax numbers, bank accounts and income evidence vary slightly between posts.
